lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: geometry and measurement

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: A rental charges a $10 base fee plus $5 per hour, totaling $35. Which equation models this, and how many hours were rented?

steps: Identify what the problem is asking and which quantities, assumptions, or constraints matter.
Build and solve a model, then check the result against the context.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A diver starts at the surface (0 m) and descends 5 m, then descends another 10 m, then ascends 22 m. The dive plan assumes a depth limit of 31 m below the surface. What is the diver's final position, as a signed number of meters?
A model predicts a $160 rate will increase by 25%. What does the model predict as the new rate?
A storage container is designed as a rectangular prism 12 ft long, 11 ft wide, and 5 ft high. What is its volume in cubic feet?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set has the values 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. The mean is 40. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD), a measure of the data's uncertainty or spread?
A student claims a box that is 6 by 5 by 5 units has a volume of 30 cubic units. Evaluate the claim.
choices: No; the volume is 150 cubic units, not 30.
No; the volume is 32 cubic units, not 30.
Cannot be determined from the given information.
No; the volume is 31 cubic units, not 30.

items.prompt: A rental company charges a $15 base fee plus $7 per hour. A customer's total bill was $127. Which equation models this situation, and how many hours were rented?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A diver starts at the surface (0 m) and descends 4 m, then descends another 11 m, then ascends 15 m. The dive plan assumes a depth limit of 22 m below the surface. What is the diver's final position, as a signed number of meters?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A model predicts a $900 rate will increase by 10%. What does the model predict as the new rate?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
